one_liner: CUDA GPU+CPU 3D Delaunay triangulator from NUS (I3D 2014), 6-9x faster than single-threaded CGAL 4.2 on scanned models.
what_it_does: gDel3D computes the full 3D Delaunay triangulation of a point set in one batch call: construct a GpuDel object (optional GDelParams), call compute(points, &output), and read back flat host arrays of tetrahedra (4 vertex indices each), face-adjacency (TetOpp), per-tet status flags and a list of failed vertices. It is not a CGAL replacement API: there is no incremental insert/remove, point location, constrained or weighted (regular) triangulation, and the repository builds only a demo executable plus a DelaunayChecker that tests Euler characteristic, orientation, adjacency and the empty-sphere property.
how_it_is_fast: Phase 1 runs on the GPU and alternates massively parallel point insertion (each tetrahedron inserts the uninserted point nearest its circumcenter) with parallel bilateral 2-3/3-2 flipping, which leaves fewer than 0.05% of facets locally non-Delaunay. Phase 2 repairs those few on the CPU with an adaptive version of Shewchuk's star splaying that rebuilds only the stars of failed vertices. Robustness comes from Shewchuk's adaptive exact orientation/insphere predicates ported to CUDA plus simulation of simplicity; fast and exact checks run in separate kernels with shared-memory compaction so that the rare exact cases do not cause warp divergence. Points are Hilbert-curve sorted for coalesced access, and a flip-history DAG is used to relocate uninserted points after flipping.
when_to_use: One-shot Delaunay tetrahedralization of 10^5 to a few 10^6 points on a machine with an NVIDIA GPU, where the paper reports 6.1-9.2x over sequential CGAL 4.2 on 173K-3.6M point scanned models

Point sets in general position, or ones you can jitter: on two raw 100K-point photogrammetry clouds a 1e-6 jitter cut gDel3D's A100 time from 0.47 s and 1.08 s to about 0.09 s (5-12x, derived from DelaunayBench page data) and removed all flat tetrahedra
Research or offline meshing pipelines where you can vendor and patch CUDA code and run the bundled DelaunayChecker on every output
Python workflows through the third-party pyGDel3D binding (half-potato/pyGDel3D), which DelaunayBench built with CUDA 12.8 on an A100
when_not_to_use: Small inputs (up to a few hundred points) on unpatched upstream code: DelaunayBench found that it silently returns the unflipped insertion result (8-12 points), hangs (32 points) or aborts on an assertion (48 and 200 points); counts matched CGAL from 505 points up
No NVIDIA GPU, or a current GPU without editing the build: CMakeLists.txt hard-codes sm_30/sm_35 and issue #11 reports 'no kernel image is available for execution on the device' on an RTX 2060
Very large clouds on modest VRAM: the code preallocates arrays for 8.5 tetrahedra per input point, and issue #6 reports an illegal memory access at 10M points on an 8 GB GPU

Strongly degenerate input (coplanar LiDAR/photogrammetry, grids) where downstream code cannot tolerate zero-volume tetrahedra: DelaunayBench counted 14,980 and 48,889 extra flat tetrahedra over CGAL on two raw 100K-point clouds
Production code that needs maintenance or a multi-core CPU baseline: last commit 2018-03-26, open issues unanswered, and the published speedups are against one CPU core

integration.dependencies: NVIDIA CUDA toolkit with Thrust; Shewchuk's predicates are bundled (CPU/predicates.cpp). CMake 2.8+ (FindCUDA) on Linux or the Visual Studio 2012 project on Windows
integration.min_toolchain: CUDA 7.5 (commit 'Compiles with CUDA 7.5 now'), CUDA 9.1 fixed in 2018; newer Thrust needs #include <thrust/device_malloc.h> added (issue #10, user workaround)
integration.platforms: NVIDIA GPUs only (README: compute capability 1.1+, best on Fermi or later; tested on GTX 450-580 under Windows and GTX Titan under Linux). Default build targets only sm_30/sm_35, so newer architectures need the gencode lines changed
integration.thread_safety: not documented (each GpuDel object owns its device buffers; the demo calls cudaSetDevice and cudaDeviceReset itself)

gotchas: Small-input correctness bug in upstream GpuDelaunay.cu: active sets under 64 tetrahedra are deferred to a 'last round' of flipping that only runs once an insertion round inserts fewer than 10% of the points. DelaunayBench's patch_pygdel3d_final_flip.py runs that round unconditionally, and upstream issue #14 (2023, unanswered) shows the same 5-tetrahedra cube

The output contains an extra 'kernel' vertex appended at index N (the input size; coordinates in output.ptInfty), and tetVec contains dead slots. Discard tetrahedra that reference it and check the alive flag in tetInfoVec before using the mesh

Degenerate input is handled by symbolic perturbation, so coplanar or cospherical points yield valid but zero-volume tetrahedra and much slower runs (the exact-arithmetic and star-splaying share grows; the paper's sphere distribution is dominated by splaying)
Double precision is the default; defining REAL_TYPE_FP32 switches all coordinates to float
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Use HXT (in Gmsh) when you only have CPUs, need more than a few million points or want maintained code: it is about 3x sequential CGAL on one core and scales across cores (10M points in 4.48 s vs CGAL's 20.15 s on a 64-core Xeon Phi). Pick gDel3D only when an NVIDIA GPU is available, the point set fits in VRAM, the input is reasonably non-degenerate, and you can patch an unmaintained CUDA codebase. The other geometry siblings (TG, nanoflann, rtree.c, mesh-boolean libraries) solve different problems.
verified_claims_summary: The peer-reviewed I3D 2014 paper (shipped in the repo) times gDel3D on an NVIDIA GTX 580 with an Intel i7-2600K (3.4 GHz, 16 GB) against sequential CGAL 4.2 on the same PC; the only build detail given is 'compiled with optimization enabled'. On uniform, Gaussian, thin-sphere, grid and cospherical sets up to 1.5M points the speedup starts at 4-6x and rises to 8-10x; on seven scanned models (173K-3.6M points) it is 6.1-9.2x, for example 3.61M-point Asian Dragon in 5.4 s. This compares one GPU against one CPU core, with a CGAL release that is now more than ten years old.
status_note: Abandoned (6 commits, last 2018-03-26, maintainer silent on issues since 2019) but BSD-3-Clause and small enough to vendor; expect to patch the CUDA arch flags, a Thrust include and the small-input flipping bug before use on a current toolkit.
